im2sim.losses.SSIMLoss#

class SSIMLoss(max_val=None, filter_size=11, filter_sigma=1.5, k1=0.01, k2=0.03, batch_dims=None, image_dims=None, rank=None)[source]#

Bases: Module

Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) loss.

The SSIM loss is defined as 1 - SSIM, where SSIM is the Structural Similarity Index Measure[1].

\[ \begin{align}\begin{aligned}\operatorname{SSIM}(x, y) = \frac{ (2\mu_x\mu_y + C_1) (2\sigma_{xy} + C_2) }{ (\mu_x^2 + \mu_y^2 + C_1) (\sigma_x^2 + \sigma_y^2 + C_2) }\\C_1 = (k_1 \, \mathrm{max\_val})^2, \qquad C_2 = (k_2 \, \mathrm{max\_val})^2.\end{aligned}\end{align} \]

rank specifies the number of image dimensions over which SSIM is calculated. The dimensions before the channel dimension are treated as batch dimensions.

This allows, for example, 2D SSIM to be calculated independently over every slice of a 3D image.

Parameters:

  • max_val (Optional[float]) – Dynamic range of the images. If None, defaults to 1 for floating-point inputs and the largest representable positive value for integer inputs.

  • filter_size (int) – Size of the Gaussian filter. Must be a positive odd integer. Defaults to 11.

  • filter_sigma (float) – Standard deviation of the Gaussian filter. Defaults to 1.5.

  • k1 (float) – Factor used to calculate the luminance regularisation constant. Defaults to 0.01.

  • k2 (float) – Factor used to calculate the contrast regularisation constant. Defaults to 0.03.

  • batch_dims (Optional[int]) –

    Number of dimensions before the channel dimension that should be treated as batch dimensions. If None, it is inferred from image_dims and the input tensor rank.

  • image_dims (Optional[int]) –

    Number of spatial dimensions used for calculating SSIM. If None, it is inferred from batch_dims and the input tensor rank.

  • rank (Optional[int]) –

    Number of spatial dimensions used by the Gaussian filter. Must be 2 or 3. If None, it is inferred from image_dims. If both are None, it defaults to 2.

Examples

Standard 2D SSIM:

>>> loss = SSIMLoss()

>>> y_true.shape == (B, C, H, W)
>>> y_pred.shape == (B, C, H, W)

3D SSIM:

>>> loss = SSIMLoss(rank=3)

>>> y_true.shape == (B, C, D, H, W)
>>> y_pred.shape == (B, C, D, H, W)

2D SSIM applied independently to every slice of a 3D image:

>>> loss = SSIMLoss(
>>>     rank=2,
>>>     batch_dims=2,
>>> )

>>> y_true.shape == (B, C, D, H, W)

>>> # B and D are treated as batch dimensions.
>>> # H and W are used as the SSIM image dimensions.

References

[1]

Zhao, H., Gallo, O., Frosio, I., & Kautz, J. (2016). Loss functions for image restoration with neural networks. IEEE Transactions on computational imaging, 3(1), 47-57.
